root_cause.text: The TX timeout handler (`bcmgenet_timeout`) unnecessarily reset and re-enabled all transmit queues upon a single queue timeout, introducing race conditions with other queues that were still actively transmitting.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes the handler from iterating over all queues (`for (q = 0; q <= priv->hw_params->tx_queues; q++)`) and calling `bcmgenet_tx_reclaim_all(dev)` and `netif_tx_wake_all_queues(dev)` to only operating on the specific timed-out queue (`ring = &priv->tx_rings[txqueue]`) with targeted reclaim, interrupt re-enable, and wake queue calls. This directly addresses the described "over zealous" behavior causing race conditions.

candidates.rationale: This loop iterates over all TX queues, causing unnecessary reset and re-enable operations on queues not involved in the timeout, introducing race conditions.
Dumps all TX queues even though only one queue timed out, resetting actively transmitting queues.
Reclaims all TX queues, disrupting ongoing transmissions on queues not experiencing a timeout.
Second loop over all queues to construct interrupt mask, ensures all queues are re-enabled regardless of which queue timed out.
Accumulates interrupt enable bits for every queue, leading to enabling interrupts for queues that were not problematic.
Writes interrupt mask that clears all queue interrupts, re-enabling interrupts for queues that may still be actively transmitting and thus causing race conditions.
Wakes all TX queues, including those that were not stopped, leading to overlapping transmissions and race conditions.
